responsibility: Define how product specifications correspond to maintained implementation, including level-to-source correspondence, source ownership, maintained versus generated source, specification coverage, implementation status, test and validator ownership, product-defined source layouts, language and build profiles, generated source treatment, partial implementation, and intentionally unimplemented specification behavior.

level_to_source_correspondence.description: Each product specification at Level 0 through Level 3 may declare correspondence to maintained source files. Correspondence binds specification constructs to implementation artifacts.

source_ownership.description: Every maintained source file must have an explicit ownership attribution identifying the specification or specification set it implements.

maintained_source.description: Source files that are hand-authored and directly maintained in the repository. Maintained source is the primary implementation artifact.

generated_source.description: Source files produced by a generator from maintained inputs. Generated source must be traceable to its generator and inputs.

specification_coverage.description: The extent to which specification constructs are implemented by maintained or generated source. Coverage may be complete, partial, or intentionally unimplemented.

implementation_status.description: The status of specification implementation, which may be fully-implemented, partially-implemented, not-implemented, or intentionally-unimplemented for each specification construct.

test_ownership.description: Tests are owned by the specification or specification set they validate. Test ownership is distinct from source ownership.

validator_ownership.description: Validators are owned by the specification or specification set whose rules they enforce. Validator ownership is distinct from source and test ownership.

product_defined_source_layout.description: A product repository may define its own source layout within the framework source area. The layout must be explicitly declared.

language_profile.description: A product profile may declare the programming language and associated conventions for its source files. Language conventions extend but do not redefine generic source correspondence rules.

build_profile.description: A product profile may declare the build system and conventions for building its source files. Build conventions extend but do not redefine generic source correspondence rules.

partial_implementation.description: A specification may be partially implemented. Partial implementation must be explicitly declared with the implemented and unimplemented portions identified.

intentionally_unimplemented_behavior.description: Specification behavior that is intentionally not implemented must be explicitly declared as intentionally unimplemented, with rationale.

specification_has_implementation_status.description: Every specification construct may declare an implementation status. The status indicates whether the construct is implemented, unimplemented, or intentionally unimplemented.

source_file_has_ownership.description: Every maintained source file must declare which specification it implements. Source files without ownership declaration are invalid.

generated_source_has_provenance.description: Every generated source file must declare its generator and inputs. Generated source without provenance is invalid.

test_validator_ownership_separate.description: Test ownership and validator ownership are distinct from source ownership. A single artifact may have different owners for source, test, and validator roles.

maintained_source.description: Hand-authored source files that are directly edited and maintained in the repository. Maintained source is the authoritative implementation of specification constructs.

generated_source.description: Source files produced by a deterministic generator from maintained inputs. Generated source may be regenerated and must not be hand-edited.

source_correspondence_is_explicit.rationale: Implicit source correspondence undermines traceability and auditability. Every specification construct that has an implementation must declare its implementing source files. Every source file must declare which specification it implements.

no_universal_layout.rationale: Different product domains use different source layouts, languages, and build systems. The framework defines generic source correspondence rules but must not require one particular layout, language, or build system.

generated_source_traceability.rationale: Generated source that cannot be traced to its generator and inputs is indistinguishable from hand-authored source. Traceability ensures that generated content can be regenerated and its provenance verified.

ownership_separation.rationale: Source ownership, test ownership, and validator ownership serve different purposes. A specification may be implemented by one source file, tested by a different file, and validated by a third. Collapsing these roles reduces accountability.

profiles_extend_not_redefine.rationale: Language and build profiles add product-specific conventions but must not override generic source correspondence rules. This prevents profile-specific semantics from leaking into the portable framework.

expected_relationships: AI-continuity model (source context for session recovery)
unresolved_questions: Concrete source-correspondence declaration format is not defined.
Implementation status vocabulary and valid values are not defined.
Generated source provenance record format is not defined.
Language and build profile schema definitions are not defined.
Partial implementation boundary declaration format is not defined.
